from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        self.setup_layout("The Legend and the Logic", [
            "Meet the Towers of Hanoi puzzle: three pegs, 'n' disks.",
            "Move all disks to the final peg following two rules.",
            "One disk at a time; never place larger on smaller."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_PEG = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_SMALL = "#FF5733"
        COLOR_MED = "#33FF57"
        COLOR_LARGE = "#3357FF"
        COLOR_CROSS = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Meet the Towers of Hanoi puzzle: three pegs, 'n' disks.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Pegs (Vertical lines from Row B to Row E)
        peg_a = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["E2"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        peg_b = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["E4"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        peg_c = Line(self.grid["B6"], self.grid["E6"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        
        # Labels for Pegs
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PEG)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PEG)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=24, color=COLOR_PEG)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "F6")

        # Disks (Placed on Peg A initially)
        # We'll use RoundedRectangle for disks
        disk_large = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.8, height=0.6, color=COLOR_LARGE, fill_opacity=1)
        disk_med = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.3, height=0.6, color=COLOR_MED, fill_opacity=1)
        disk_small = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.8, height=0.6, color=COLOR_SMALL, fill_opacity=1)

        # Place disks on Peg A (Column 2)
        # Note: We stack them vertically in rows E, D, C
        self.place_at_grid(disk_large, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(disk_med, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(disk_small, "C2")

        # Execution
        self.play(
            Create(peg_a), Create(peg_b), Create(peg_c),
            Write(label_a), Write(label_b), Write(label_c)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(disk_large), FadeIn(disk_med), FadeIn(disk_small))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Move all disks to the final peg following two rules.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animation: Move Smallest disk from Peg A to Peg C
        # It goes from C2 to E6
        self.play(disk_small.animate.move_to(self.grid["E6"]))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animation: Move Medium disk from Peg A to Peg B
        # It goes from D2 to E4
        self.play(disk_med.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # One disk at a time; never place larger on smaller.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Invalid Move Attempt: Large disk tries to go on top of Medium disk on Peg B
        # Target position is above medium disk on Peg B (D4)
        target_pos_invalid = self.grid["D4"]
        
        # Create a red cross
        cross = Cross(stroke_color=COLOR_CROSS, stroke_width=20)
        self.place_at_grid(cross, "D4", scale_factor=0.6)

        # Large disk moves to Peg B
        self.play(disk_large.animate.move_to(target_pos_invalid))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show failure and return
        self.play(FadeOut(cross), disk_large.animate.move_to(self.grid["E2"]))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section data
        title = "Prerequisite: The Binary Heartbeat"
        lines = [
            "Binary counting acts like a rhythmic visual odometer.",
            "Each move flips specific bits in a repeating cycle.",
            "The rightmost bit changes every single step."
        ]
        
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_white = WHITE
        color_highlight = "#FFFF00" # Yellow for bits that change

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the binary sequence '0 0 0' in #FFFFFF at screen center.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_white)
        
        # Creating digits separately to allow individual animation
        # Scale digits initially so we can refer to their scale later
        d1 = MathTex("0", color=color_white)
        d2 = MathTex("0", color=color_white)
        d3 = MathTex("0", color=color_white)
        binary_digits = VGroup(d1, d2, d3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        
        # Position the binary sequence in the visual area (right side)
        self.place_in_area(binary_digits, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=3.0)
        
        self.play(Write(binary_digits))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Increment to '0 0 1' and flash the rightmost digit in #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Create the new '1' digit with the same scale as the group's children
        d3_new = MathTex("1", color=color_highlight).scale(3.0).move_to(d3)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(d3, shift=UP*0.3),
            FadeIn(d3_new, shift=UP*0.3),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.play(Flash(d3_new, color=color_highlight, line_length=0.4))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Increment to '0 1 0' and flash the middle digit in #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_highlight)
        
        # Update d3 back to 0 and d2 to 1
        d3_final = MathTex("0", color=color_white).scale(3.0).move_to(d3)
        d2_new = MathTex("1", color=color_highlight).scale(3.0).move_to(d2)
        
        self.play(
            # d3 goes from 1 back to 0
            FadeOut(d3_new, shift=UP*0.3),
            FadeIn(d3_final, shift=UP*0.3),
            # d2 goes from 0 to 1
            FadeOut(d2, shift=UP*0.3),
            FadeIn(d2_new, shift=UP*0.3),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.play(Flash(d2_new, color=color_highlight, line_length=0.4))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Magic Mapping Rule"
        lines = [
            "Every binary change dictates which disk to move.",
            "Identify the rightmost bit that changed in the move.",
            "Bit position determines the disk number to move.",
            "Move 1 flips bit 1: move disk 1.",
            "Move 2 flips bit 2: move disk 2."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        DISK_COLORS = {
            1: "#FF5733", # Orange-Red
            2: "#33FF57", # Green
            3: "#3357FF"  # Blue
        }
        HL_COLOR = YELLOW

        # Helper to create binary bits
        def create_binary_group(bits_str):
            group = VGroup()
            for char in bits_str:
                group.add(Text(char, font="Monospace", font_size=48))
            group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
            return group

        # Helper to create disks
        def create_disks():
            d1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=0.8, fill_opacity=0.8, color=DISK_COLORS[1], fill_color=DISK_COLORS[1])
            d2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=DISK_COLORS[2], fill_color=DISK_COLORS[2])
            d3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.4, width=1.6, fill_opacity=0.8, color=DISK_COLORS[3], fill_color=DISK_COLORS[3])
            
            l1 = Text("Disk 1", font_size=18).next_to(d1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            l2 = Text("Disk 2", font_size=18).next_to(d2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            l3 = Text("Disk 3", font_size=18).next_to(d3, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            
            return VGroup(VGroup(d1, l1), VGroup(d2, l2), VGroup(d3, l3)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)

        # Initial Setup
        binary_counter = create_binary_group("000")
        self.place_in_area(binary_counter, "B2", "B5")
        
        disks = create_disks()
        self.place_in_area(disks, "E1", "E6")

        bit_labels = VGroup(
            Text("Bit 3", font_size=16, color=GRAY).next_to(binary_counter[0], UP),
            Text("Bit 2", font_size=16, color=GRAY).next_to(binary_counter[1], UP),
            Text("Bit 1", font_size=16, color=GRAY).next_to(binary_counter[2], UP)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HL_COLOR))
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_counter), FadeIn(disks), FadeIn(bit_labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HL_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Transition 000 -> 001
        new_binary_1 = create_binary_group("001")
        self.place_in_area(new_binary_1, "B2", "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(binary_counter[2], new_binary_1[2]),
            binary_counter[2].animate.set_color(HL_COLOR),
            bit_labels[2].animate.set_color(HL_COLOR)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HL_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Link Bit 1 to Disk 1
        link = Line(binary_counter[2].get_bottom(), disks[0][0].get_top(), color=HL_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        glow = link.copy().set_stroke(width=8, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(link), FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(Indicate(disks[0][0], color=DISK_COLORS[1]))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(link), FadeOut(glow), binary_counter[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), bit_labels[2].animate.set_color(GRAY))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HL_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Show Highlight for Disk 1
        self.play(
            binary_counter[2].animate.set_color(DISK_COLORS[1]),
            disks[0][0].animate.scale(1.2).set_stroke(YELLOW, 3),
        )
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            binary_counter[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            disks[0][0].animate.scale(1/1.2).set_stroke(width=0),
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HL_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Transition 001 -> 010
        new_binary_2 = create_binary_group("010")
        self.place_in_area(new_binary_2, "B2", "B5")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(binary_counter[1], new_binary_2[1]),
            Transform(binary_counter[2], new_binary_2[2]),
        )
        
        self.play(
            binary_counter[1].animate.set_color(DISK_COLORS[2]),
            bit_labels[1].animate.set_color(DISK_COLORS[2])
        )
        
        link2 = Line(binary_counter[1].get_bottom(), disks[1][0].get_top(), color=DISK_COLORS[2], stroke_width=4)
        self.play(Create(link2))
        self.play(Indicate(disks[1][0], color=DISK_COLORS[2]))
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(link2),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Directional Parity: Where does the disk go?", [
            "Where should the disk go? Follow the parity rule.",
            "For odd disks, move disk 1 in clockwise steps.",
            "For even disks, move disk 1 in counter-clockwise steps."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        PATH_COLOR = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        PEG_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use white color for the first line initially
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create three pegs in a circular layout
        # Peg A: Top (C3)
        # Peg B: Bottom Right (E5)
        # Peg C: Bottom Left (E1)
        peg_a = Circle(radius=0.4, color=PEG_COLOR)
        peg_b = Circle(radius=0.4, color=PEG_COLOR)
        peg_c = Circle(radius=0.4, color=PEG_COLOR)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "E5")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "E1")
        
        # Labels for pegs (offset to avoid paths as per B009)
        label_a = Text("Peg A", font_size=20).next_to(peg_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_b = Text("Peg B", font_size=20).next_to(peg_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        label_c = Text("Peg C", font_size=20).next_to(peg_c, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        pegs_group = VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c, label_a, label_b, label_c)
        self.play(FadeIn(pegs_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PATH_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Total Disk Parity Label (Rule Trigger)
        # Use Row B to avoid Row A (B005) and preserve grid center
        odd_label = Text("Total Disks: ODD", font_size=24, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(odd_label, "B1", "B6")
        self.play(Write(odd_label))
        
        # Clockwise Arrows (A -> B -> C -> A)
        arrow_ab = CurvedArrow(peg_a.get_right(), peg_b.get_top(), radius=-2, color=PATH_COLOR)
        arrow_bc = CurvedArrow(peg_b.get_left(), peg_c.get_right(), radius=-2.5, color=PATH_COLOR)
        arrow_ca = CurvedArrow(peg_c.get_top(), peg_a.get_left(), radius=-2, color=PATH_COLOR)
        
        arrows_cw = VGroup(arrow_ab, arrow_bc, arrow_ca)
        self.play(Create(arrows_cw))
        
        # Small Disk 1
        disk1 = Circle(radius=0.15, color=PATH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        disk1.move_to(peg_a.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(disk1))
        
        # Move disk 1 in Clockwise steps
        # Move Along Path ensures it follows the arcs correctly
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(disk1, arrow_ab))
        self.wait(0.2)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(disk1, arrow_bc))
        self.wait(0.2)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(disk1, arrow_ca))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Update Parity Label to EVEN
        even_label = Text("Total Disks: EVEN", font_size=24, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(even_label, "B1", "B6")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(odd_label, even_label))
        
        # Reverse Arrows for Counter-Clockwise (A -> C -> B -> A)
        arrow_ac = CurvedArrow(peg_a.get_left(), peg_c.get_top(), radius=2, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        arrow_cb = CurvedArrow(peg_c.get_right(), peg_b.get_left(), radius=2.5, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        arrow_ba = CurvedArrow(peg_b.get_top(), peg_a.get_right(), radius=2, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        arrows_ccw = VGroup(arrow_ac, arrow_cb, arrow_ba)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrows_cw),
            Create(arrows_ccw)
        )
        
        # Move disk 1 in Counter-Clockwise steps
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(disk1, arrow_ac))
        self.wait(0.2)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(disk1, arrow_cb))
        self.wait(0.2)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(disk1, arrow_ba))
        self.wait(2)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Fractal Path", [
            "Disk movements trace a beautiful, hidden fractal path.",
            "The state space forms a perfect Sierpinski Triangle.",
            "Binary counting maps a perfect Hamiltonian path through it."
        ])
        
        # Color definitions
        FRACTAL_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        PATH_COLOR = YELLOW
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a simple triangle connecting three points labeled as puzzle states.
        # Anchor points for the main triangle
        v1 = self.grid["B3"]
        v2 = self.grid["E1"]
        v3 = self.grid["E5"]
        
        main_triangle = Polygon(v1, v2, v3, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        # State labels near vertices (Constraint: within 1 unit)
        label1 = MathTex("S_0", font_size=24, color=FRACTAL_COLOR)
        label2 = MathTex("S_1", font_size=24, color=FRACTAL_COLOR)
        label3 = MathTex("S_2", font_size=24, color=FRACTAL_COLOR)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "F1", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label3, "F5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Match lecture line color
        self.lecture[0].set_color(FRACTAL_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(main_triangle), Write(label1), Write(label2), Write(label3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Subdivide the triangle into four smaller ones to begin the fractal.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(FRACTAL_COLOR)
        
        # Midpoints of the main triangle
        m12 = (v1 + v2) / 2
        m23 = (v2 + v3) / 2
        m31 = (v3 + v1) / 2
        
        # Three corner triangles forming the first level of the fractal
        t1 = Polygon(v1, m12, m31, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        t2 = Polygon(v2, m12, m23, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        t3 = Polygon(v3, m23, m31, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(main_triangle),
            Create(t1), Create(t2), Create(t3),
            FadeOut(label1), FadeOut(label2), FadeOut(label3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Second level of subdivision
        tris_lv2 = VGroup()
        for p in [(v1, m12, m31), (v2, m12, m23), (v3, m23, m31)]:
            sm12 = (p[0] + p[1]) / 2
            sm23 = (p[1] + p[2]) / 2
            sm31 = (p[2] + p[0]) / 2
            tris_lv2.add(Polygon(p[0], sm12, sm31, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, stroke_width=1.5))
            tris_lv2.add(Polygon(p[1], sm12, sm23, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, stroke_width=1.5))
            tris_lv2.add(Polygon(p[2], sm23, sm31, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, stroke_width=1.5))

        self.play(FadeOut(t1), FadeOut(t2), FadeOut(t3), Create(tris_lv2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Trace a path through the vertices as the binary counter increments rapidly.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(FRACTAL_COLOR)
        
        # Binary Counter UI (Bit representation)
        counter_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        counter_label = Text("Binary Counter:", font_size=20).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_label, "A1", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Bits: 6 rectangles to avoid recreating Text in updater
        bits = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.3, height=0.2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=1) for _ in range(6)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(bits, "A3", scale_factor=1.0).shift(RIGHT * 0.5) # Shift slightly away from label

        def update_bits(mob):
            val = int(counter_tracker.get_value())
            bin_str = bin(val)[2:].zfill(6)
            for i, bit in enumerate(bin_str):
                if bit == "1":
                    mob[i].set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8)
                else:
                    mob[i].set_fill(BLACK, opacity=0)
        
        bits.add_updater(update_bits)
        self.add(counter_label, bits)

        # Representative Hamiltonian Path points
        path_points = [
            v1, (v1+m12)/2, m12, (v2+m12)/2, v2, 
            (v2+m23)/2, m23, (v3+m23)/2, v3, 
            (v3+m31)/2, m31, (v1+m31)/2, v1
        ]
        path_segments = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(path_points)-1):
            path_segments.add(Line(path_points[i], path_points[i+1], color=PATH_COLOR, stroke_width=3))

        # Trace the path and increment counter
        self.play(
            counter_tracker.animate.set_value(63),
            Create(path_segments),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Transition to multi-level Sierpinski Gasket (Zoom out simulation)
        def get_gasket(order, side, center):
            if order == 0:
                return Polygon(
                    center + UP*side, 
                    center + LEFT*side*0.866 + DOWN*side*0.5,
                    center + RIGHT*side*0.866 + DOWN*side*0.5,
                    stroke_width=0.5, color=FRACTAL_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3
                )
            else:
                s = side/2
                return VGroup(
                    get_gasket(order-1, s, center + UP*s),
                    get_gasket(order-1, s, center + LEFT*s*0.866 + DOWN*s*0.5),
                    get_gasket(order-1, s, center + RIGHT*s*0.866 + DOWN*s*0.5)
                )

        multi_level_gasket = get_gasket(4, 2.2, self.grid["D3"])
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(tris_lv2),
            FadeOut(path_segments),
            FadeIn(multi_level_gasket)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Final Transition: Fade fractal into Towers of Hanoi solution view
        pegs = VGroup(
            Line(DOWN, UP).shift(LEFT*0.6),
            Line(DOWN, UP),
            Line(DOWN, UP).shift(RIGHT*0.6)
        ).set_color(GREY_B)
        
        base_line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT).scale(0.8).next_to(pegs, DOWN, buff=0)
        
        disks = VGroup(
            Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.15, color=RED, fill_opacity=1),
            Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.15, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1),
            Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.15, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=1)
        ).arrange(UP, buff=0.05).move_to(pegs[0].get_bottom() + UP*0.1)
        
        hanoi_demo = VGroup(pegs, base_line, disks)
        self.place_in_area(hanoi_demo, "C2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(multi_level_gasket),
            FadeOut(counter_label),
            FadeOut(bits),
            FadeIn(hanoi_demo)
        )
        
        # Illustrate the relationship by moving a disk
        self.play(
            disks[2].animate.move_to(pegs[2].get_bottom() + UP*0.1),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Binary Rhythms: Solving the Towers of Hanoi with Binary Counting
outline.target_audience: High school or early university computer science and math students

sections.title: The Legend and the Logic
sections.content: Introduce the Towers of Hanoi puzzle: 3 pegs and 'n' disks of different sizes. Explain the goal (move all disks to the last peg) and the two strict rules: move only one disk at a time, and never place a larger disk on a smaller one. Present the puzzle as a sequence of moves that follows a hidden mathematical rhythm.
sections.example: Visualize a 3-disk puzzle. To move the stack, it takes exactly 7 moves ($2^3 - 1$). Imagine a small robot named 'Bit' attempting to solve it but getting confused by the recursive steps.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Binary Heartbeat
sections.content: Introduce binary counting as a visual 'odometer'. Explain that in binary, the rightmost bit flips every step, the second bit every two steps, and the third every four steps. This section builds the foundation for mapping these 'flips' to disk movements.
sections.example: An animation showing a 3-bit counter: 001, 010, 011, 100... Highlight the 'rightmost bit that changes' in each step. For example, moving from 011 (3) to 100 (4) changes the 3rd bit from the right.

sections.title: The Magic Mapping Rule
sections.content: Connect the binary counter to the disks. The rule is simple: In move 'm', identify the rightmost bit that changed in the binary representation of 'm'. The position of that bit (1st, 2nd, or 3rd) tells you exactly which disk to move (Disk 1, Disk 2, or Disk 3).
sections.example: On Move 1 (001), the 1st bit changes -> Move Disk 1. On Move 2 (010), the 2nd bit is the rightmost change -> Move Disk 2. On Move 3 (011), the 1st bit changes again -> Move Disk 1.

sections.title: Directional Parity: Where does the disk go?
sections.content: Introduce the 'Cyclic Rule' for placement. For a set of disks, Disk 1 always moves in one direction (A -> B -> C -> A) if the total number of disks is odd, and the other way if even. This eliminates the 'which peg?' guesswork.
sections.example: Visualizing Disk 1 as a fast-moving 'scout' jumping pegs in a clockwise circle, while larger disks follow a slower, counter-clockwise rhythm. If Disk 1 is on Peg A and needs to move, it *must* go to Peg B based on the parity rule.

sections.title: Visualizing the Fractal Path
sections.content: Summarize the relationship between binary counting and the Sierpinski Triangle. Show that the state space of the Towers of Hanoi actually forms a fractal. When you follow the binary counting method, you are tracing a Hamiltonian path along the edges of a Sierpinski Gasket.
sections.example: The camera zooms out from the 3-disk puzzle to show a 6-disk puzzle. As the binary counter counts rapidly, the movements trace a perfect triangular fractal shape on the screen, showing the beauty of mathematical efficiency.
